title: Utility Theory of Synthetic Data Generation
summary: Builds a theory of when synthetic data is useful, separating the utility of a downstream model trained on synthetic rows into a term for how well the generator approximates the real distribution and a term for the downstream task itself, and shows that closing the distributional gap is sufficient without requiring the generator to be consistent everywhere. The empirical program rests entirely on SDV: CopulaGAN, GaussianCopula, CTGAN and TVAE are the four generators the theory is instantiated on, each trained at varying sample sizes and scored through a downstream linear SVM.
evidence: the simulation section states that four generative models are considered, Copula GAN attributed to Patki et al. 2016, Gaussian Copula, CTGAN from Xu et al. 2019, and TVAE, with a linear SVM as the downstream task; Figure 3 plots the utility measure under varying training sample sizes with a panel for each of Copula GAN, Gaussian Copula, VAE and CTGAN

title: Distributed Conditional GAN (discGAN) For Synthetic Healthcare Data Generation
summary: Proposes discGAN, a distributed conditional GAN for synthetic electronic health records, in which discriminators sit with the data at each site so that patient records never leave their holder, evaluated on ICU stay records by machine-learning efficacy, Kolmogorov-Smirnov and chi-squared tests. CTGAN is the state of the art the design is written against: the literature survey gives it its own section headed as the conditional tabular model from the Synthetic Data Vault, the paper takes its account of the discrete-and-continuous modelling problem from it, and discGAN's architecture is defined by contrast, dropping the residual block the CTGAN implementation uses. CTGAN itself is not run.
evidence: the literature survey section II.A is headed CTGAN: Modeling Conditional Tabular Data from Synthetic Data Vault and describes it as the state-of-the-art tabular generator from MIT; the model section states the paper uses methods described in the CTGAN reference to produce single-table synthetic data and quotes its account of simultaneously modelling discrete and continuous columns; the architecture subsection states discGAN forewent adding residual blocks, opposed to the SOTA CTGAN implementation; no experiment trains or samples CTGAN

title: Synthpop++: A Hybrid Framework for Generating A Country-scale Synthetic Population
summary: Builds Synthpop++, a country-scale synthetic population for India that layers four data sources of differing granularity, using iterative proportional updating where marginals exist and a learned generator where they do not, and validating the result against held-out survey distributions. CTGAN supplies the attributes marginals cannot reach: it is trained on Individual and Household microdata and conditioned on age and sex to attach weight, height, comorbidities and job description to each synthetic person, and the paper selects it over statistical alternatives for handling mixed types, high dimensionality and imbalanced categoricals.
evidence: the method section states that matching only marginal distributions is not enough and that CTGAN is used for adding individual-level attributes for which marginals are not available, noting the model can be conditioned on attributes already present in the base population; a later passage states that for weight, height and comorbidities a CTGAN model conditioned on age and sex is used, trained on the subset of the IHDS-II dataset for Maharashtra, with Individual and Household microdata as CTGAN input

title: Diverse Community Data for Benchmarking Data Privacy Algorithms
summary: Publishes a set of curated excerpts from American Community Survey data, chosen so that privacy algorithms can be tested on small, tractable populations whose subgroup structure is visible, and pairs them with an evaluation suite that surfaces defects aggregate utility scores hide. CTGAN, listed as the SDV implementation, is one of the synthesizers run across the excerpts as the non-differentially-private neural comparator, and the analysis reports it failing to preserve constraints that hold for child records and dropping a housing-feature constraint.
affiliations: National Institute of Standards and Technology
evidence: Table 1 lists SDV CTGAN among the evaluated deidentification methods, categorised as non-DP synthetic data from a generative adversarial network, with its reported utility and subsample percentages; the results discussion states that CTGAN is not preserving constraints that hold for child records and is missing a constraint on housing features, alongside a propensity and PCA comparison of the three neural synthesizers
